remaining_open_items: Firmware and peripheral protocols are not simulated.
GPIO alternate-function/type mapping and power-sequence rules remain application-specific.
Board thermal path and programmed I/O state require explicit circuit context.
CIO 5pF is typical, not a worst-case maximum; no maximum can be inferred from guaranteed-by-design footnote.

Former simulation blocker resolved for the bound reference (2026-10-11, D075): No validated interface-only recipe; firmware execution is not simulable. Resolution: ST DS8626 Rev 12 (ST-hosted, archived) gives the reset state (all I/Os floating inputs during and after reset unless bracketed or noted, p48), the five-volt-tolerant structure of every pin (Table 7), the absolute maxima including the FT input limit and injection limits (Tables 11-13, p80-81), the I/O static characteristics (Table 48, p116-117), the NRST pull-up (Table 51, p121) and thermal resistance (Table 98, p185). The part is bound as its electrical pins in that reset state; firmware is not modeled. The recorded LQFP144 pin map was cross-checked against the Table 7 LQFP144 column and agrees.
The debug pins PA13, PA14, PA15, PB3 and PB4 come out of reset in their JTAG/SWD function; DS8626 does not state their pulls, so they are not modeled.
PC13-PC15 depend on the backup domain after reset (Table 7 note 4) and are not modeled.
Core, regulator and peripheral supply current is not modeled (Table 20 values recorded only).
Output drive is reachable only through a future explicit pin-state declaration.

simulation_reason: Simulates as the bound reference part (STM32F407ZGT6 / STM32F407ZGT6 LQFP144): electrical pins in reset state only; firmware not modeled. The package alone has no electrical function, so results describe that part in this package.
